title: Citrus stimulus vocabulary v1: modes, families, colour representation and appearance rules

consumers.rule: generated from this document by verify_stimulus_vocabulary.py --emit-python, never hand-copied

color_space.meaning: Display-referred drive values as written to the stimulus framebuffer. Not linear light, not measured luminance.

color.authored: RGBA floats in [0, 1] (Citrus ImVec4 / colour-module value).

optional.color_name: lowercase ASCII string; present only when the producer asserts a name

rgba8_round_half_up_v1.rule: x is the authored channel as Citrus holds it, IEEE binary32 (ImVec4, colour picker, CUDA kernels), promoted exactly to double; v = x * 255 evaluated as an IEEE double; u8 = clamp(round_half_away_from_zero(v), 0, 255) per channel (C lround semantics: exact .5 rounds away from zero, never to even); non-finite x -> 0. With binary32 inputs the only exact .5 tie is x = 0.5 (127.5 -> 128); every other one- or two-decimal value lands just above or below the tie on the binary32 side, which is why 0.3 -> 77 but 0.7 -> 178.
rgba8_round_half_up_v1.not_this: Quantising the decimal as a double is NOT this rule: double 0.7 * 255 is exactly 178.5 and gives 179, while the binary32 nearest 0.7 (0.699999988) gives 178.499997 -> 178, which is what Citrus displays and records. Python round() (half to even) on the double 0.3 gives 76; floor(v + 0.5) differs from lround for v just below .5 (0.49999999999999994 -> 1 instead of 0).
rgba8_round_half_up_v1.citrus: CitrusColor::QuantizeChannelRoundHalfUpV1 (src/color/color.h): std::lround(double(float x) * 255.0) clamped; used by protocol_trial_index.cpp Color() and the SOLID_COLOR fill. Device: object_appearance_contrast.cuh QuantizeCodeValueToU8V1 = floor(double(x) * 255.0 + 0.5) clamped, which is exactly lround for binary32 x (the product and the sum are exact in double); before citrus #28 it was float32 (x * 255.0f + 0.5f) and gave 179 for 0.7f and 230 for 0.9f. tests/test_object_appearance_contrast_device.cu replays the decimal rows on the GPU against the host rule.
rgba8_round_half_up_v1.palette: src/fisheye/shared/color_quantization.py: unit_to_u8 / unit_rgba_to_rgba8, QUANTIZATION_ID = rgba8_round_half_up_v1 (replaces the four half-to-even sites; replays fixtures/resolved_color_examples.json; Palette commit 5fea6a36, pins this document at agent-contracts 880a5ed); MUST convert the authored decimal to binary32 (struct.pack('f') / numpy.float32) before multiplying, see verify_stimulus_vocabulary.py binary32()

rgba8_trunc_legacy.rule: x is the authored binary32 channel promoted to double; u8 = clamp(trunc(x * 255), 0, 255) per channel
rgba8_trunc_legacy.citrus: MovingGratingStimulus.cu and ScrollingGridStimulus.cu kernels before the colour-module migration
rgba8_trunc_legacy.consumer_rule: Palette never recomputes a displayed code from authored floats for elements quantised this way; a backfill records the displayed code as absent rather than guess. Pre-citrus-#29 recordings (before 2026-10-13) displayed truncated / float-lround codes that were never recorded; never recompute a pre-#29 displayed code from authored floats. The v2 trial-index fields (line_color, bg_color, flash colours, chasers[k].color) are authored, pre-brightness codes and remain valid as authored values.

color.modifier_rule: Brightness and alpha are authoring inputs folded in before quantisation. The recorded rgba8 is the code written to the framebuffer. No field named luminance, intensity or brightness ever holds a code value.
color.physical_claim: rgba8 is a display drive value, not measured luminance. Measured light, once a photodiode exists, is a separate rig-calibration record keyed by (rig, rgba8); it never rewrites these fields.
solid_invariants: color_name == "black" if and only if rgba8 == [0, 0, 0, 255] on a solid_color step
color_name == "white" if and only if rgba8 == [255, 255, 255, 255] on a solid_color step
SOLID_BLACK (4) requires color_type_id 0 and rgba8 [0, 0, 0, 255]; SOLID_WHITE (5) requires color_type_id 1 and rgba8 [255, 255, 255, 255]
SOLID_COLOR (22): color_name is "gray" when r == g == b and the code is neither black nor white; otherwise color_name is omitted; never "black" or "white" unless the code is exactly that

columns./components/visual_appearance/states: reference_rgba, realized_rgba: float32[4] = displayed code / 255 (every producer). code = V1(stored) recovers all 256 codes; float32(k/255) * 255 is a non-integer in double for 254 of the 256 codes, so never truncate and never use the raw product.
columns./components/moving_grating/states: line_color_rgba, background_color_rgba: float32[4] = authored RGB * brightness (RGB) and authored alpha, before quantisation; brightness: float32.

h5_per_frame_columns.reading_rule: code = V1(stored float) = clamp(lround(double(stored) * 255), 0, 255) per channel. For the moving_grating columns this equals the displayed code only for files whose trial index is v3 with features.appearance.elements (citrus >= 9ba1744, #29); for every other file the grating columns are authored values whose displayed code was rgba8_trunc_legacy (and the first frame ignored brightness) and is never recomputed.
h5_per_frame_columns.keyed_on: the file itself: /protocol/authored trial index schema_version == 3 and steps[*].features.appearance.elements present; not on producer history or dates. Option 2 (a /metadata/session display_color_quantization attribute) was considered and not taken.
h5_per_frame_columns.fact: No rig file was written with trial index v3 between citrus #27 (576481f, 2026-10-12) and #29 (883a639, 2026-10-13): pancake0's GUI binary stayed at cf7a60b (pre-#27) because the rebuild was held. Therefore 'trial index v3 with elements' identifies producers at or after #29, and the first GUI rebuild must ship at least c52ac4e + #29 + #30 (element derivation), never #27 alone.
h5_per_frame_columns.never: Never recompute a pre-#29 displayed grating code from the stored floats; never recompute any displayed code from a decimal without rounding to binary32 first.

solid_color.features.color_name: black|white for modes 4 and 5; for mode 22 optional: black, white or gray (r == g == b, neither black nor white) when the displayed code is exactly that, else absent
solid_color.features.resolved_color: recorded_form, exact displayed code (mode 22: rgba8_round_half_up_v1 of the authored colour)

moving_grating.features.line_color: rgba8 of the AUTHORED floats, pre-brightness
moving_grating.features.bg_color: rgba8 of the AUTHORED floats, pre-brightness
moving_grating.features.brightness: float multiplier; displayed code was truncated (rgba8_trunc_legacy)

chaser.features.appearance: object_appearance_profile digest and policy ids when a profile is set

v3_rules: LIVE IN CITRUS since citrus 576481f (#27, 2026-10-12): top-level stimulus_angle_convention = atan2_negative_y_x_degrees and normalization_policy citrus.protocol.trial_index.v3. Since citrus 9ba1744 (colour step 2, 2026-10-13) every presentation mode carries features.appearance.elements, and a minimal step may carry features.appearance alone (schema digest f23c20a7... since citrus 2f3a482, which adds the required element derivation). consumer_accepts stays [1, 2] until Palette's v3 PR merges: until then Citrus main writes what Palette rejects, and no rig recording may be admitted on v3. Since citrus 8525697 (static phototaxis redesign) mode 18 is detailed with features.region / fill / brightness (schema digest 33659c8d...).

features.appearance.elements.<element> = {authored_color {color_space: srgb, rgba: binary32 floats}, brightness, derivation, quantization, resolved_color, contrast_profile_digest|null} for every presentation mode. resolved_color is the code the stimulus writes to the framebuffer; derivation (appearance.element_derivations) names the rule that produces it from authored_color and brightness, so a consumer recomputes and checks every element without a prose table.

Element names: solid_color: background (== features.resolved_color); moving_grating / concentric_grating: line, background (grating brightness folded in; the v2 line_color/bg_color stay pre-brightness); flash: baseline, flash (opaque: RGB clamped to [0,1], alpha 255); coherent_dots / concentric_dots / moving_dots / looming_dot: dot, background (coherent: brightness on the dot only; concentric: background premultiplied by its alpha, displayed opaque); phototaxis: side_a (inside the region) and side_b (elsewhere) for fill two_tone, or gradient_from and gradient_to (the endpoint codes, not the colour of every pixel) for fill gradient; features.fill carries type, domain, outside_area_policy (side_b_v1 | masked_black_v1) and, for gradient, formula_id linear_srgb_gradient_v1, axis, start_fraction, end_fraction; features.region and features.brightness are recorded; since citrus's phototaxis static fill redesign (2026-10-13) the mode is detailed and its semantic identity includes colours, brightness and fill; spotlight: spot, background (opaque); static_image / scrolling_grid / static_grid / independent_motion_grid: background, plus border when a grid shows borders (image texels are not authored colours); chaser: chaser_<k> (k = chaser_index; contrast_profile_digest = the appearance profile digest when set), background, background_edge_minimum (when the edge falloff is on: the background code times minimum_brightness, +0.5 truncated; brightness = minimum_brightness), proximity and danger_zone when enabled.

Solid steps (modes 4, 5, 22) keep features.color_name and features.resolved_color through at least one transition version, and features.appearance.elements.background.resolved_color == features.resolved_color (alias rule). Palette switches its solid-black classifier to the elements path before Citrus may drop the old fields.

Spatially varying fills are recorded as the elements that bound them plus the existing per-mode feature that describes the profile: the chaser background edge falloff is elements background (plain_v1) and background_edge_minimum (edge_minimum_floor_half_v1) plus features.background_edge_falloff (profile, minimum_brightness, falloff_width_fraction); the endpoints are not the displayed colour of every pixel between them. There is no fill field in the element. appearance.fill_formula_ids stays reserved (planned) for a future gradient stimulus.
Per-frame H5 colour fields (grating line/background, appearance reference/realized) move to the recorded form with an admission bump agreed with Palette; that is separate from the trial-index bump.
Gate: no rig recording is ADMITTED on trial index v3 until Palette lands v3 support and bumps consumer_accepts; Citrus main writes v3 now (the gap the verifier prints).

SOLID_COLOR 22 LIVE (this revision, 2026-10-14, at Jeremy's direction: the importer must accept the mode, no substitution by SOLID_BLACK/SOLID_WHITE): protocol parameters color_type Custom + color {color_space: srgb, rgba}; trial index features.resolved_color (recorded_form of the displayed code), features.color_name only when the code is exactly black, white or gray, and features.appearance.elements.background (brightness 1, plain_v1, rgba8_round_half_up_v1, no contrast profile) with elements.background.resolved_color == features.resolved_color. Citrus has written this since b470de2 (#28). Effective for admission once Palette regenerates its mirror from this revision, merges and re-pins live intake.

Trial index v3 schema digest 61f6c573... (Citrus PR 2 of the reactive phototaxis track, 2026-10-14): mode 18 fill.type gains heading_split with fill.style and features.reactive, present exactly when fill.type is heading_split (agent-contracts citrus-palette/reactive_phototaxis revision 5). Static two-tone and gradient steps are unchanged.

consumer_accepts moved to [1, 2, 3] in the 2026-10-14 revision: Palette's live intake (f31ea0e8, admission revision 5) accepts trial index v3 under the angle_v1 binding; Palette does not vendor this file, the field records the consumer state.

phototaxis_geometry.frame: stimulus-canvas raster pixels: origin top-left, x to the right, y DOWN. TOP is the smaller y. The experimental area centre (cx, cy) and the circle radius r are canvas pixels (PHOTOTAXIS_START event details: experimental_center_x_px/y_px, circle_radius_px).
phototaxis_geometry.pixel_convention: A raster pixel (i, j) is drawn with its centre (i + 0.5, j + 0.5), for the region test, the experimental-area test and the gradient axis position alike. Arithmetic is binary32.

region_rule.note: inclusive at the dividing lines: a point exactly on the centre line belongs to the region whichever side is named, and the centre point belongs to every quarter. side_a is drawn where the rule holds inside the experimental area; side_b elsewhere (outside_area_policy side_b_v1).

phototaxis_geometry.gradient_axis_rule: axis x runs left to right and axis y runs top to bottom (increasing canvas y); start_fraction < end_fraction measure along that direction over the experimental area's extent (axis_min = centre - extent/2; a circular area spans 2 r).
phototaxis_geometry.consumer_rule: Classify a fish (or any camera-frame position) by mapping it through the camera-to-canvas homography into canvas pixels and applying region_rule; never by camera-image side or camera-image top/bottom. On a reflected rig (negative homography determinant, e.g. omnifin0) canvas TOP is camera BOTTOM and camera-image halves would invert side_a without error.
phototaxis_geometry.cross_reference: citrus-palette/angles plane rule (only map through the homography; the orientation agent's unit-circle convention is the angle counterpart of this position rule).
phototaxis_geometry.citrus: src/stimuli/phototaxis_region.cuh InsideRegion / PixelCentre (used by the kernel and replayed by tests/test_protocol_trial_index.cpp PhototaxisRegionRule).

appearance.brightness: One scalar multiplier per element, authored in [0, 1], recorded beside the authored colour; resolved_color is post-brightness.

contrast_profile.scope_rule: scope_id identifies the element the profile applies to (today: chaser objects; generalised to any figure-over-ground element by widening the scope enum, which is an admission note, not a table-shape change). The H5 table /components/visual_appearance/states is keyed by (stimulus_frame_num, scope_id).

linear_srgb_gradient_v1.meaning: per-pixel linear interpolation of two authored colours along an axis in the srgb drive domain, brightness folded in, quantised per pixel. Used by PHOTOTAXIS fill gradient (citrus >= the commit in producer.commit).
linear_srgb_gradient_v1.rule: Endpoints folded as plain_v1: fb_c = binary32(from_c * brightness), tb_c = binary32(to_c * brightness) for RGB, fb_a = from_a, tb_a = to_a. Pixel position p = pixel index + 0.5 along the axis (x or y, raster pixels); u = (p - axis_min) / axis_extent where axis_min/axis_extent are the experimental area's minimum edge and extent along the axis (a circular area spans 2 r); t = clamp((u - start_fraction) / (end_fraction - start_fraction), 0, 1). c_c = fb_c + (tb_c - fb_c) * t; code_c = clamp(floor(c_c * 255 + 0.5), 0, 255), literally floor of (c * 255 + 0.5) on the computed double c: NOT lround (they differ only at c * 255 = 0.49999999999999994, which floor-half maps to 1; implement floor-half literally, do not simplify). All of u, t, c and the final scale are IEEE double operations on the binary32 inputs promoted exactly, each operation rounded individually (no FMA; the Citrus device path uses the _rn intrinsics). At t = 0 the code is V1(fb) and at t = 1 it is V1(tb) exactly, so the recorded elements gradient_from / gradient_to are the true endpoint codes. Outside the experimental area the pixel is masked black [0,0,0,255].
linear_srgb_gradient_v1.citrus: src/color/linear_srgb_gradient.cuh (GradientT, GradientCodeV1), PhototaxisStimulus.cu kernel; tests/test_color.cpp and the GPU harness (phototaxis_gradient_matches_formula) replay every pixel against the host formula.

element_derivations.precision: Authored channels and brightness are binary32; every product of two binary32 values is rounded back to binary32 before the next step (as Citrus computes it in float); V1 = rgba8_round_half_up_v1 (binary32 promoted to double, times 255, lround, clamp); the edge-minimum scale is computed in double, where an 8-bit code times a binary32 and the +0.5 are exact (no float32 re-rounding, no FMA).

plain_v1.elements: every element not listed under another id

opaque_alpha_v1.rule: rgb as plain_v1; a = 255 (the stimulus displays the colour opaque and ignores the authored alpha)
opaque_alpha_v1.elements: flash: baseline, flash (RGB clamped to [0,1] by the stimulus before display; authored_color records the clamped value); spotlight: spot, background

premultiplied_background_v1.rule: rgb_c = V1(binary32(binary32(c * a) * brightness)); a = 255 (the background is composited over black by its own authored alpha before quantisation and displayed opaque)

edge_minimum_floor_half_v1.rule: code = V1(c) with no brightness; rgb_c = floor(double(code_c) * double(brightness) + 0.5), clamped to [0,255]; a = code_a. brightness is the falloff's minimum_brightness; pixels between this ring and the plain background follow features.background_edge_falloff (smoothstep of the same scale)

compatibility.adding_a_mode: Append to modes with status planned; Citrus may then define it (the verifier accepts a planned mode present in the Citrus enum, and refuses any id the document does not list); Palette pins the new document and its generated mirror; status becomes live only after the Palette intake pin passes the commit that reads it. Ids are never reused or renumbered.
compatibility.changing_a_family_or_name: A new schema_version of this document; consumers fail closed on an unknown version.
compatibility.changing_quantization: A new quantization id, carried per element in the trial index; never a silent change of an existing id's rule.
